stories.title: Downtown Phoenix Luxury Hotel to Debut September 16
stories.excerpt: Pacific Hospitality Group (PHG) is taking reservations for its latest hotel, the Denu Hotel & Spa in downtown Phoenix. The 236-room hotel is at 1 E. Adams Street in downtown Phoenix in a newly constructed 17-story building. Features include the Hammam-inspired spa, the Solstone Holistic Spa offers thermal rituals and immersive treatments; a fitness and wellbeing program; a rooftop pool with sweeping city views; and versatile meeting and event spaces designed to accommodate everything from corporate gatherings to celebratory social occasions. Denū is located steps from major transportation hubs, the convention center and the city’s arts, culture, sports and entertainment venues. A lobby-level restaurant and lounge, café and rooftop bar complete the experience. PHG operates both branded and independent resort properties. The company manages, develops, finances, and owns hotels and resorts in California, Hawaii, Arizona and Texas. PHG currently owns and manages 11 hotels and resorts, representing over 2,463 rooms and 185,791 square feet of indoor meeting and event space. bullets: Pacific Hospitality Group opens 236-room Denu Hotel in downtown Phoenix, September 2026.
New 17-story luxury hotel near convention center, arts venues, transit hubs.
Rooftop pool, spa, restaurant, meeting space target corporate and leisure travelers.
stories.summary: Pacific Hospitality Group is opening Denu Hotel & Spa, a 236-room luxury property at 1 E. Adams Street in downtown Phoenix. The 17-story building features high-end amenities including a spa, rooftop pool, restaurant, and 185,791 square feet of meeting space. The location sits adjacent to major transit, the convention center, and cultural venues.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Hotel supply does not compete for or consume residential land in downtown Phoenix, though it signals confidence in downtown's visitor economy and may support mixed-use residential projects via street-level activation and urban amenities.

stories.title: ALDI Reveals Westward Expansion
stories.excerpt: As ALDI enters its 50th year in the United States, the low-price grocer is doubling down on its nationwide expansion, announcing plans to open more than 180 stores by the end of 2026. ALDI is announcing expansion plans into the state of Colorado within the next five years, with more than 50 stores planned for Denver and Colorado Springs. As ALDI continues its westward expansion, the grocer will open 10 new stores in the Phoenix market in 2026 and plans to add a total of 40 new stores by the end of 2030. After debuting four stores in 2025, the grocer will continue to deepen its presence in the growing market with plans to double its current store count by 2030. Additionally, the chain will open two distribution centers in the SW, one in Goodyear, Arizona (projected 2028)and the other in Aurora, Colorado (projected 2029) The post ALDI Reveals Westward Expansion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ALDI plans 180+ new stores by end of 2026; 40+ stores in Phoenix by 2030.
Two regional distribution centers planned: Goodyear, Arizona (2028) and Aurora, Colorado (2029).
Entry into Colorado with 50+ stores planned for Denver and Colorado Springs by 2031.
stories.summary: ALDI announced its largest expansion push with 180+ new stores planned by end of 2026, including 40 stores in the Phoenix market and 50+ in Colorado (Denver and Colorado Springs). The grocer will also build two regional distribution centers—one in Goodyear, Arizona (2028) and one in Aurora, Colorado (2029)—to support westward growth. ALDI opened four Phoenix stores in 2025 and plans to double its footprint there by 2030.
stories.impact: Major retail infill and logistics investment signals sustained population and household growth in Phoenix and Colorado Front Range metros. Distribution center employment and retail job creation will drive labor in-migration and household formation, strengthening multifamily rent growth and leasing velocity in both markets. Goodyear DC alone will anchor significant wage-earning workforce; developers should acquire residential land near these logistics nodes (Goodyear, Aurora) for mixed-income and workforce housing.

stories.title: Mamdani Sets Sights on Fixing — Not Replacing — Deteriorating Section of BQE
stories.excerpt: Will Mayor Zohran Mamdani be the first administration to finally fix the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights? Mamdani announced Monday morning that the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) would build bypasses around the surrounding neighborhoods and maintain access to local attractions while finally rebuilding the swiftly deteriorating cantilever portion of the freeway. DOT would build a two-level bypass above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, sitting below the promenade and not extending above the current highway. The city would also create a second elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge. The Mamdani administration plans to start the estimated $4 billion project in 2030, despite a sense of urgency from officials. The city estimates the project could take 10 years. The Mamdani administration said it believes this renovation, as opposed to a replacement, will extend the life of the BQE for another 40 years. “After decades of kicking the can down the road and indecision that failed to yield substantial results, we will act with urgency to rehabilitate the city’s portion of the BQE to ensure the safety of New Yorkers and minimize the likelihood of massive traffic diversions into Brooklyn neighborhoods,” DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. “While the city and the state must right the wrongs of Robert Moses with the BQE and other infrastructure plowed through urban communities, decades of political paralysis have left us out of options.” For every year that the city procrastinates, costs increase by an estimated $160 million, according to the announcement. “For decades, prior administrations have failed to deliver urgent long-term repairs to BQE Central — but we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We’re going to fix the aging concrete, repair the deteriorating triple cantilever and build temporary roads that keep the highway operabl
bullets: NYC DOT plans $4 billion Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) rehabilitation starting 2030.
Project duration estimated at 10 years; will extend BQE life another 40 years.
Two-level bypass construction to maintain local access and preserve Brooklyn Promenade.
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration announced a $4 billion plan to rebuild the deteriorating cantilever section of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) via a rehabilitation (not replacement) strategy. The DOT will construct two elevated bypasses—one above Furman Street and another from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge—with construction starting in 2030 and expected to take 10 years.
stories.impact: Moderate indirect impact on Brooklyn Heights and Nolita residential development. A decade-long BQE construction project (2030–2040) will degrade traffic and accessibility in adjacent neighborhoods, likely suppressing near-term lease-up and rent growth in proximate multifamily projects. However, the long-term infrastructure upgrade should improve Brooklyn Heights air quality and street-level conditions post-2040, potentially unlocking waterfront residential development and higher rents in the outer years. Developers with projects in Brooklyn Heights face headwinds during construction; timing new deliveries post-2040 may be optimal.

stories.title: Kinsmen Property Group Plans to Bring 322 New Homes to 156-166 Bowery
stories.excerpt: Kinsmen Property Group, a New York City-based real estate development and investment firm, has big plans to build 322 homes along the Bowery in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. After previously filing plans to demolish a 15,000-square-foot set of vacant buildings at 156-166 Bowery in October 2024, Kinsmen has now filed a land use application with the Department of City Planning to transform the now-vacant lot into three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings with a total of 322 homes, according to the firm. If approved, the three buildings would comprise a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors; a 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 3,260 square feet of ground-floor retail space; and another 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 4,391 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The project, which would be designed by architects Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter public review through a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) by the end of the year. “We are excited to bring more than 300 new homes to Lower Manhattan at a time when housing is urgently needed across the city,” Ari Zagdanski, principal of Kinsmen, said in a statement. “This project is designed to honor the rich history of the Bowery while also addressing the city’s housing needs head-on.” The site at 156-166 Bowery has already been through various different planned projects. In 2022, previous owner Real Estate Equities Corporation (REEC) — which had signed a 99-year ground lease for the properties in 2020 for $50 million — filed plans to construct a seven-story, 73,000-square-foot retail and office building on the site. Construction on that project eventually stalled. It’s unclear whether REEC still owns the ground lease at the Nolita site, which Kinsmen bought in a set of separate purchases in 2016 and 2017 for a total of $53.5 million, according to records. bullets: Kinsmen Property Group plans 322 apartments at 156-166 Bowery, Nolita, Manhattan.
Project includes 124 affordable senior units, 198 mixed-income units, 7,651 SF retail.
Three buildings (29, 26, 26 stories) expected to enter ULURP public review by year-end.
stories.summary: Kinsmen Property Group filed a land use application to develop 156-166 Bowery in Manhattan's Nolita neighborhood into three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings totaling 322 apartments. The project comprises a 29-story tower with 124 affordable senior units, and two 26-story towers with 99 mixed-income units each and 7,651 square feet of ground-floor retail. The development, designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter ULURP by end of 2025.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued Manhattan density play in historically transit-poor, lower-density neighborhoods. Nolita infill development—especially 300+ units with senior and mixed-income components—indicates developer confidence in Bowery-area demand and lender appetite for complex deal structures (affordable components, mixed-income). ULURP approval timing will be watched; if approved and fast-tracked, this signals zoning flexibility in lower Manhattan and may encourage similar speculation in underbuilt East Village/Bowery submarkets.

stories.title: Front Street Eyeing 8.4M-SF Lexington, NC Industrial Development
stories.excerpt: Front Street Capital is pursuing an 850-acre master-planned industrial park in the city of Lexington. The city annexed the land to accommodate the project, but it still needs to create and approve zoning for the project. The Triad Business Journal reports Front Street’s current concept for the park includes 15 parcels ranging in size from 11 acres to 153 acres. The site offers potential for around 8.4 million square feet of industrial space, with buildings ranging from 80,000 to 2 million square feet. The project is designed to accommodate advanced manufacturing, logistics firms and corporate campuses that have multiple buildings. The property’s close access to I-85 and Norfolk Southern rail lines. Front Street is also partnering with other investors on The Grounds mixed-use development in Winston-Salem. The $250 million first phase will have a student apartment complex, a 135,000-square-foot office building and a 42,000-square-foot retail village. The post Front Street Eyeing 8.4M-SF Lexington, NC Industrial Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Front Street Capital planning 8.4M-SF industrial park on 850-acre site in Lexington, NC.
15 parcels ranging 11–153 acres; buildings 80K–2M SF; accommodates advanced manufacturing, logistics.
Project access to I-85 and Norfolk Southern rail; zoning approval still pending.
stories.summary: Front Street Capital is pursuing a master-planned 850-acre industrial park in Lexington, North Carolina, with potential for 8.4 million square feet across 15 parcels (11–153 acres). The site is designed for advanced manufacturing, logistics, and multi-building corporate campuses, with direct access to Interstate 85 and Norfolk Southern rail lines. The city has annexed the land, but zoning approval is still required.
stories.impact: Large logistics and manufacturing hub signals major job creation and labor migration into the Greensboro-Lexington Triad, lifting regional employment base and household formation. Front Street's concurrent $250M investment in The Grounds mixed-use in Winston-Salem (student apartments, office, retail) suggests coordinated regional density strategy. Multifamily developers should acquire sites in Lexington and nearby Greensboro for workforce and market-rate housing to capture migrating logistics/manufacturing workforce; proximity to I-85 and rail access will attract employer tenants and support residential pre-leasing.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Arranges $250M Refinancing for 506-Unit Seattle MF
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged a $250 million refinancing for Museum House, a newly completed 506-unit multifamily community in Seattle, Washington. The Cushman & Wakefield Equity, Debt & Structured Finance team of Dave Karson, Christopher Moyer, Alex Lapidus and Meredith Crawford represented the sponsor, a pension fund, in arranging the financing. Barings provided the loan. “This is one of the most architecturally significant buildings in Seattle, and the First Hill neighborhood is developing nicely as a residential community just outside the downtown,” said Dave Karson, Executive Vice Chair at Cushman & Wakefield. Completed in 2025, Museum House features 506 studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences, including 404 market-rate apartments and 102 income-restricted affordable homes. The property also includes 6,010 square feet of ground-floor retail. Located in Seattle’s First Hill neighborhood, Museum House is adjacent to the Frye Art Museum and offers convenient access to downtown Seattle, Capitol Hill, Seattle University, healthcare institutions and regional transit. Join the industry’s top multifamily decision-makers at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Hear from the investors, developers, lenders, owners, and advisors shaping today’s apartment market through candid conversations, networking, and market insights. bullets: Cushman & Wakefield arranged $250M refi for Museum House, 506-unit completed property in Seattle.
Project includes 404 market-rate, 102 affordable units, 6,010 SF retail; located First Hill neighborhood.
Barings provided loan; sponsor is pension fund; property completed 2025.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield secured a $250 million refinancing from Barings for Museum House, a newly completed 506-unit multifamily community in Seattle's First Hill neighborhood. The property comprises 404 market-rate and 102 affordable apartments (studios through three-bedroom), plus 6,010 square feet of ground-floor retail. Completed in 2025, the architecturally distinctive project sits adjacent to the Frye Art Museum and offers walkable access to downtown, Capitol Hill, and Seattle University.
stories.impact: Strong capital market signal for Seattle multifamily: institutional lender (Barings) willing to finance 506 units at $494K per unit on a just-completed, mixed-income property indicates robust Seattle credit and lender confidence in First Hill's residential trajectory. First Hill's emergence as a residential neighborhood outside downtown (rather than office/medical campus) opens development window for additional mid-rise multifamily. Developers should prioritize First Hill and adjacent Capitol Hill-adjacent sites for pre-leasing and acquisition; First Hill's healthcare/university proximity and transit access support premium rent growth and institutional tenant demand.

stories.title: Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project
stories.excerpt: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health are moving forward with plans for a new teaching hospital at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW, which will include a network of primary, urgent and specialty care designed to reach communities across Central and South Fulton County. Atrium Health is committing more than $700 million in capital and clinical investment to the hospital and broader care network. The goal is to bring a Level III trauma center with more care closer to where people live. Plans include an acute care hospital, primary care practices, locations combining primary and urgent care, specialty services, virtual and community-based care and a healthplex offering services such as imaging, infusion, endoscopy and emergency care. The new hospital is planned to open with approximately 50 beds with the ability to expand to over 700 beds over time as community needs grow. It will deliver 24/7 emergency and Level III trauma, obstetrics and a neonatal intensive care unit, adult critical care, advanced imaging, cardiac catheterization, interventional radiology and endoscopy. The post Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health committing $700M to new teaching hospital in Fulton County, Georgia.
Level III trauma center at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW; opening ~50 beds, expandable to 700+.
Planned services include emergency care, obstetrics, ICU, cardiac, imaging; phased development.
stories.summary: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health are advancing a $700 million teaching hospital project in Central/South Fulton County, Georgia, anchored at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW. The facility will open with approximately 50 acute-care beds, expandable to 700+ over time, and will deliver a Level III trauma center, emergency services, obstetrics, neonatal ICU, and specialty services across a network of primary care, urgent care, and virtual care locations.
stories.impact: Significant anchor employer and job creation catalyst for South Fulton County. Atrium's $700M investment in primary care, urgent/specialty care, and teaching hospital will drive physician recruitment, healthcare professional in-migration, and sustained job growth across clinical and support roles. Developers should acquire multifamily sites within 2–3 miles of 675 Metropolitan Parkway for workforce and physician housing; South Fulton's historical underinvestment means early-mover advantage for residential near this anchor. Hospital expansion trajectory (50 to 700 beds) suggests phased workforce growth over 5–10 years, supporting staged residential absorption.

stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty closed 37,600 SF new leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 W. 34th St), Midtown Manhattan.
Bohler Engineering expanded to 14,000 SF (10-year lease at $67/SF); T&M USA took 14,000 SF.
Tenants cited central transit access and first-class property as drivers.
stories.summary: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 square feet of new leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 West 34th Street) in Midtown Manhattan. The two largest deals were Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 to 14,000 square feet on a 10-year lease at $67/SF, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which leased 14,000 square feet. Tenants cited transportation access and property quality as decision factors.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development. Office leasing activity in Midtown does not directly affect residential demand or supply dynamics, though sustained engineering and tech office tenancy signals continued employment in Manhattan's prime office corridor, supporting downstream residential demand in nearby transit-accessible neighborhoods (e.g., Hudson Yards, Hell's Kitchen, Murray Hill).

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. Construction might have slowed down in other sectors, but the explosive growth of data centers has seemingly made up for it, at least according to a recent report from Skanska. “The market is hot and cold right now — hot and warm may be a better way to say it — so what stands out is that we’re seeing a lot of project activity around data centers, semiconductor, life sciences,” said Skanska’s Tom Park. “There’s really a lot of unprecedented demand in the mechanical, electrical, plumbing and steel space driving up lead times and cost.” Moreover, the companies that rely on the proliferation of data cent
bullets: Data center sector attracting $1.3 trillion in capital investment; Coreweave raised $23B debt from 38 lenders.
Non-bank lenders (PIMCO, others) originating billions; PIMCO alone $23B in originations.
Major borrowers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle) driving AI/compute infrastructure spending.
stories.summary: The U.S. data center sector is attracting an estimated $1.3 trillion in capital investment as of 2026, with massive individual financings like Coreweave's $23 billion debt facility backed by 38 lenders and DigitalBridge/IFM's $20 billion facility. Non-bank lenders such as PIMCO have originated $23 billion in data center financing. Tech giants Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Oracle are driving the investment wave through sustained AI and computational infrastructure demand.
stories.impact: Indirect but significant: Massive data center capex cycles concentrate high-wage employment in cluster markets (Northern Virginia, Texas, Arizona, Northern California, Midwest). Downstream effect lifts office and multifamily demand in data center hubs. Developers should monitor regional data center announcements and secure land near new data center clusters for tech workforce housing; these sites absorb premium rent from high-income ICT workers and show resilient lease-up even in macroeconomic downturns.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar closed $800M acquisition of Zonda, new-home data and homebuilder software platform.
Zonda generated ~$170M revenue in 2025; serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers.
Platform provides lot-level development data; CoStar gains foothold in $400B new-home market.
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a platform providing lot-level construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace tools. Zonda serves over 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers and generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. The acquisition gives CoStar access to the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market and proprietary development data.
stories.impact: Moderate strategic signal: CoStar's vertical integration into homebuilder data and workflows may accelerate consolidation of real estate information platforms, improving data transparency and capital allocation efficiency for developers and lenders. Enhanced lot-level development visibility and standardized data could lower acquisition and underwriting friction, enabling faster deployment of capital into residential development. Multifamily developers using CoStar/Zonda tools will see improved market intelligence on competing single-family supply and land availability, sharpening site selection and demand forecasting in suburban and exurban markets.
